title: Health Checks Men Skip
hook: Men see doctors less and die younger from preventable causes. A handful of simple checks catch the big risks early.
key_points: Men use preventive care less than women, often waiting until something hurts.
Get blood pressure checked regularly; high BP usually has no symptoms.
Know your cholesterol and blood sugar to catch heart and diabetes risk early.
Colorectal cancer screening is recommended starting at age 45.
A regular clinician relationship makes it easier to act on what checks find.
content_html: Men, on average, see doctors less often than women and are more likely to wait until a problem becomes urgent. That gap shows up in worse outcomes from largely preventable conditions like heart disease and certain cancers.
extra_html:
A few routine checks catch the biggest risks before they cause harm. Blood pressure should be measured regularly because high blood pressure typically has no symptoms. Knowing your cholesterol and blood sugar numbers flags heart disease and type 2 diabetes risk early, when lifestyle changes work best. Colorectal cancer screening is recommended starting at age 45 for those at average risk.

The CDC emphasizes that prevention and early detection are far easier than treating advanced disease. Building a relationship with a regular clinician makes it simpler to stay current on these checks and to act quickly when something turns up. None of this requires feeling sick first.

source.name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

related.title: Why Regular Checkups Matter
related.hook: The whole point of a checkup is to catch trouble while it's still quiet — before symptoms show up and while it's easiest to treat.

related.title: Understanding Blood Pressure
related.hook: High blood pressure is called the 'silent killer' for a reason — it usually has no symptoms, yet it quietly raises your risk of heart attack and stroke.

related.title: Preventing Type 2 Diabetes
related.hook: Type 2 diabetes often arrives slowly, with a warning stage called prediabetes — and at that stage, modest lifestyle changes can stop or delay it.

related.title: Cancer Screenings Worth Knowing
related.hook: Screening looks for cancer before symptoms start — and for a few common cancers, that early catch dramatically improves the odds.

related.title: Prostate Health and Screening
related.hook: PSA screening for prostate cancer isn't an automatic yes. It's a genuine judgment call you make with your doctor.

flashcards.prompt: Why is regular blood pressure screening important even if you feel fine?
flashcards.back_html: High blood pressure usually causes no symptoms, so the only way to know you have it is to measure it. Left unchecked it quietly raises the risk of heart disease and stroke.

flashcards.prompt: At what age is colorectal cancer screening generally recommended to begin?
flashcards.explanation_html: Current guidance recommends starting colorectal cancer screening at age 45 for adults at average risk.
